similar_scenes.name: Pop de los setenta y power-pop
similar_scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
similar_scenes.desc: Abba, campeones del pop de los setenta, de las armonías efervescentes a la pista de baile y el melodrama romántico. Alex Chilton (Box Tops, Big Star) es el profeta del power-pop: melodía pura, armonías a cuatro voces, guitarras jingle-jangle y riffs de hard rock (Radio City); su ideología retro impregnará la new wave y el brit-pop de los noventa. Raspberries.

similar_scenes.name: American Graffiti: revival, garage y power-pop
similar_scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
similar_scenes.desc: American Graffiti (1973) desata el revival de los cincuenta y sesenta, que suenan más auténticos que el rock corporativo de los setenta: rockabilly, surf, folk-rock, psicodelia, bandas sonoras de terror. Los punks descubren el alma malvada del rockabilly: Suicide inventa el psychobilly y los Cramps el «voodoobilly»; Fleshtones, Raybeats, Stray Cats, Von Lmo. El garage revive con Slickee Boys, Pretenders, Wipers, Real Kids; el power-pop con Cheap Trick, Shoes, Cars, Jonathan Richman y Embarrassment. En California, los Blasters y el cow-punk de Rank And File; Tom Petty como teórico del power-pop, Plimsouls, Redd Kross, Go-Go's, Bangles. El blues para la generación punk: George Thorogood, Fabulous Thunderbirds, J. Geils Band, Dixie Dregs.

podcast.title: US Breakthrough Summer (1979)
podcast.body: The summer of 1979 in America was recognized as the breakthrough season for New Wave, during which power pop bands such as Cheap Trick, The Knack, and The Cars achieved their biggest hits to date. "that was the breakthrough summer of New Wave, as power pop bands like Cheap Trick. The neck, and the cars. All scored their biggest hits to date."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Big Star's Influence and Liner Note Grammy
podcast.body: Big Star, a cult-favorite Power Pop act from the 1970s, became a major influence on Power Pop bands globally. Despite their limited record sales, they notably received a Grammy Award for Best Liner Notes in 2013 for their box set "Keep an Eye on the Sky." "Alex Chilton and Big Star major influence on Power Pop bands everywhere."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Blue Album's Contrast to Pinkerton
podcast.body: The "Pinkerton" album was noted for not being a "grungey power pop album like the first one," indicating that Weezer's debut, "The Blue Album," was characterized by a power pop sound. "This was not a grungy power pop album like the first one."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 1

podcast.title: British and American Origins
podcast.body: While British bands such as The Beatles and their descendants Badfinger provided an initial "spark" for Power Pop, the first prominent wave of Power Pop bands were predominantly American, including groups like The Raspberries (fronted by Eric Carmen), Big Star (led by Alex Chilton), and the solo artist Todd Rundgren. "While British bands like The Beatles and their descendents Badfinger gave a spark to Powerpop, the first wave of Powerpop bands were mostly American."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Core Characteristics
podcast.body: Power Pop emerged as a "back-to-basics rock movement" that took the catchy 1960s pop sounds of bands like The Who or The Beach Boys and "turbo-charged it" with increased energy and volume. "Another back-to-basics rock movement that took catchy 60s pop by the likes of The Who or The Beach Boys and Turbo-charged it."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Early New Wave Characteristic
podcast.body: The first period of the New Wave era (roughly 1978-1984) was characterized by a jerky, twitchy, fun, and sometimes goofy style of power pop, primarily based on traditional instruments like guitars, bass, and drums. "The first featured the jerky, twitchy, fun sort of power pop that could get a little goofy from time to time. That's your standard new wave. It was based largely on guitars, bass, and drums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: End of 70s / Early 80s Appeal
podcast.body: Power pop, exemplified by The Pretenders, was highly sought after at the close of the 1970s and the beginning of the 1980s, alongside the quirky sounds of The B-52s and the genre-bending of The Police, catering to a strong appetite for change. "The goofy stuff from the B-52s and the power pop of the pretenders and the genre bending of the police were just what a lot of people were looking for at the end of the 70s in the beginning of the 80s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 1: New Wave

podcast.title: First Wave New Wave Characteristic
podcast.body: The first wave of New Wave was characterized as an energetic, guitar-based, slightly jittery brand of power pop. "The energetic guitar based, slightly jittery brand of power pop featuring people in suit jackets and skinny ties."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Alt Rock Revivals Part 5: New Wave

podcast.title: Presence in Mid-90s America
podcast.body: The middle 1990s in America saw the rise of notable power pop bands, such as Veruca Salt, featuring strong female artists. "Veruchas Salt, bookended by Nina Gordon and Louise Post. They were one of the great American power pop bands of the middle 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: Women Who Rocked The 90's

podcast.title: Subgenre of New Wave
podcast.body: Power Pop was identified as a distinct subgenre nested within the broader "New Wave" umbrella. Artists such as Elvis Costello and Tom Petty were cited as prime examples of this style, characterized by its catchy melodies and energetic delivery. "There was Power Pop, which could include everyone from Elvis Costello to Tom Petty, a new Scott Seen, a specials English beat and so on, and all of the flavors of Technopop, all those groups who threw away their guitars and favor of synthesizers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The Raspberries as Pioneers
podcast.body: The Raspberries are widely cited as a groundbreaking band and one of the first examples of the Power Pop sound, particularly in the context of early alt-rock. "Ask anyone about Power Pop, and they will talk about the raspberries."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Transatlantic Sound
podcast.body: Power Pop constituted a significant part of the "transatlantic sound" that became central to what New Wave ultimately represented, alongside England's pub rock and punk rock scenes. "the transatlantic sound of Power Pop."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
